title: Ending apartment vacation rentals and hotel rezoning of 48 properties
summary: On October 23, the Council voted down Resolutions 26-160 and 26-161, which would have sent more condo properties to the Maui Planning Commission for hotel zoning review. The chair said vacation rentals are being phased out of apartment districts, and new hotel districts exist for properties where continued rental use is appropriate. On September 29, the Council sent a list of coastal apartment-zoned properties to the Commission under Resolution 26-129, five to four.

timeline.text: Planning said it is not sure some properties meet the rule that short-term rental use began before September 24, 2020.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The committee is weighing whether to rezone certain apartment properties so short-term vacation rentals can continue.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The H3 and H4 districts match the A1 and A2 apartment districts, except short-term vacation rentals are allowed.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: Bill 88 creates new H3 and H4 hotel zoning districts.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: A condo owner testified that rezoning studies could cost $200,000 to $500,000 per property.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: A condo board president testified that all 26 owners at his complex support Bill 88.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: The Office of Hawaiian Affairs testified against Bill 88 and asked the council to defer it.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: Members amended the bill so expansion of the existing total square footage of the floor area is prohibited.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: A legal advisor said the list of possibly qualifying properties is informational and does not stop others from applying.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: Bill 88 would create H3 and H4 hotel districts that conditionally allow vacation rentals being phased out of apartment districts.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: Bill 88 would create H3 and H4 hotel districts for properties now in A1 and A2 apartment districts.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: A testifier urged the council to pass Bill 88, which creates H3 and H4 zoning, unchanged.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: The bill moves on to the full council for its consideration.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The committee voted six to one, with two members excused, to recommend passing the bill.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: That amendment passed with seven ayes and no noes.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: A second amendment leaves Molokaʻi out of the new districts, as the Molokaʻi Planning Commission asked.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: A member moved to limit the new districts to properties that already met the rules for vacation rentals in apartment districts.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: Planning staff said H3 and H4 do not add any vacation rental units.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: Another testifier said he supports the bill only if properties have security, housekeeping, a front desk and staff on site.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: A Lahaina Strong representative testified against the new zoning.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: All three planning commissions recommended denial of the bill.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: Planning staff said the new districts copy the A1 and A2 apartment district rules and do not rezone any property now.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: Planning staff said moving specific properties into H3 or H4 would be a separate, second step.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The new districts would let some apartment-zoned properties keep transient vacation rentals (short-term rentals).
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: Resolution 25-230 sends a bill creating H3 and H4 hotel districts to the Lānaʻi, Maui and Molokaʻi planning commissions.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: She said she fully supports passing the mayor's Bill 9 on short-term rentals with no exemptions.
timeline.body: County Council Special Meeting

timeline.text: The first nominee said he would prefer Bill 9 be taken up together with legislation based on a published report's recommendations.
timeline.body: County Council Special Meeting

timeline.text: A council member said the mayor's Bill 9 comes up for a vote right after this appointment.
timeline.body: County Council Special Meeting

timeline.text: A testifier urged members not to choose based on wanting one more vote for or against Bill 9.
timeline.body: County Council Special Meeting
